source_title: Peloton Interactive, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022
company_context: Peloton Interactive is a connected-fitness, direct-to-consumer company selling Bike, Bike+, Tread and Tread+ hardware plus a recurring Connected Fitness subscription. After a pandemic-era demand surge in FY2020-FY2021, demand reverted sharply as consumers returned to gyms. Peloton had built capacity and committed to supply for demand that did not materialize, producing a large inventory overhang, heavy losses, and severe operating cash burn in FY2022 that forced restructuring and management change.
business_type: Connected-fitness consumer hardware plus subscription, direct-to-consumer (DTC), asset/inventory-heavy with owned and contracted manufacturing
evidence_summary: In fiscal 2022 (ended June 30, 2022) Peloton's total revenue fell to $3.58 billion from $4.02 billion in FY2021, an 11% full-year decline, with Connected Fitness Product revenue falling from $3.15 billion to $2.19 billion as pandemic-era demand reversed. The company recorded a net loss of approximately $2.83 billion for the fiscal year. Inventory built for demand that did not materialize forced large reserves: a $123.9 million reserve as of June 30, 2022 primarily for excess accessories and apparel it did not expect to sell above cost, and $224.9 million of excess-and-obsolete inventory reserve adjustments recognized within the reconciliation of net loss to operating cash flow for the year. The company averaged roughly negative $650 million of free cash flow per quarter in the six months into Q4 FY2022, improving to about negative $412 million in Q4. The mismatch between built/committed supply and collapsed demand is the core operational-breakdown signature.

outcome_evidence: Multi-billion-dollar net loss for FY2022, double-digit revenue decline, large inventory reserves and write-downs, and sustained heavy negative free cash flow; the company entered an aggressive restructuring program (cost cuts, headcount reduction, shift from owned to outsourced manufacturing) and CEO transition during the period.

Free-cash-flow per-quarter figures are management-reported non-GAAP framing. Some figures rounded as presented.
